supplement.where: Appendix A (p. 30) and Appendix B 'Supplementary Regression Tables' (pp. 30-36) of this PDF; no external online supplement is mentioned
supplement.holds: Table A.1 quantile regressions (quantiles 0.1 to 0.9); full mixed-model tables for purchase intent and novelty with random effects, N RespondentID (200 for purchase intent, 201 for novelty), N IdeaID 400, and observations (7982 purchase intent, 8023 novelty); simple, alternative-weight, zero-shot-baseline, and ordered-logit variants

paper_design_summary: The authors compare three pools of product ideas for college students priced at $50 or less: 200 ideas sampled from a larger pool produced in a 2021 product design course with 50 students, 100 GPT-4 ideas generated through the researchers' zero-shot prompts, and 100 through their few-shot prompts. Prolific raters scored the ideas for purchase intent (quality) and novelty, and the authors measured within-pool similarity with Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings. No study participants were assigned to AI-assisted ideation.

studies.label: Studies 1-3 (one corpus of 400 ideas: students vs GPT-4 zero-shot vs GPT-4 few-shot; Study 1 quality, Study 2 similarity and novelty, Study 3 top-decile quality)

participants.who: Corpus of 400 ideas: 200 ideas randomly selected from ideas by 50 students in a 2021 product design and innovation course at 'an elite university' (no AI), plus 100 GPT-4 zero-shot and 100 GPT-4 few-shot ideas. Ideas were rated by college-age Prolific respondents from the United States (200 respondents for purchase intent, 201 for novelty, Appendix B pp. 31 and 34).
participants.country: United States (raters); students' country not stated
participants.quote: In this course, 50 students participated in an innovation challenge to come up with ideas for a physical product marketed to college students for $50 or less

ai_tool.how_used: The researchers prompted GPT-4 to generate ten ideas at a time using the students' prompt (zero-shot) or the same prompt plus six highly rated ideas from a separate student set (few-shot), and asked it to summarize earlier ideas to stay within the context window. These model-generated pools were compared with the students' pre-existing ideas; no study participants were assigned to AI-assisted ideation (pp. 10-12, Section 4).

task.description: New physical product ideas targeted at US college students, retail price under about USD 50, each a title plus a 40-80 word paragraph

contrasts.reported: Average purchase intent: 46.4% with zero-shot prompting and 49.3% with few-shot prompting vs humans 40.4%. Mixed model: zero-shot β = 0.059; 95% CI [0.031, 0.088]; t(246) = 4.06, p < 0.001; few-shot β = 0.089; 95% CI [0.060, 0.12]; t(223) = 5.93, p < 0.001. Appendix B: N RespondentID 200, N IdeaID 400, Observations 7982.
contrasts.locator: p. 13 (Section 5, text below Figure 1); p. 14 (Section 5); Appendix B pp. 30-31

contrasts.reported: Average novelty: human 40.6% (SD: 0.117), zero-shot GPT-4 36.7% (SD: 0.101), few-shot GPT-4 36.1% (SD: 0.111). Mixed model: zero-shot β = -0.038; 95% CI [-0.066, -0.01]; t(269) = -2.67, p = 0.008; few-shot β = -0.049; 95% CI [-0.078, -0.02]; t(268) = -3.4, p < 0.001. Appendix B: N RespondentID 201, N IdeaID 400, Observations 8023.

outcomes.name: Average pairwise cosine similarity within each idea pool, Study 2
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Direction refers to diversity (GPT-4 pools have higher similarity). Table 1, average cosine similarity of all ideas: Student 0.221, GPT-4 zero-shot 0.415, GPT-4 few-shot 0.428 (N ideas 200 / 100 / 100). Human vs GPT-4: η² = 0.358, 95% CI [-0.197, -0.190], F(1, 24649) = 13715.82, p < 0.001; three groups: η² = 0.455, F(2, 29598) = 12340.95, p < 0.001. Robustness, minimum spanning tree diversity: student 0.53, zero-shot 0.33, few-shot 0.3. The corpus contains 400 ideas; the number of analyzed pairs is not reported.
contrasts.locator: p. 15, Table 1 and text; p. 24, Section 8.2.2

outcomes.name: Share of the top decile of purchase intent, Study 3
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Among the top 40 ideas (top decile) 35 (87.5%) were generated by GPT-4. Table 3, fraction of the top decile of pooled ideas: Student 5/40, GPT-4 zero-shot 15/40, GPT-4 few-shot 20/40; average quality of top decile 0.62 / 0.64 / 0.66; average novelty of top decile 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.33. Chi-square x2 = 26.39, p < 0.001, df = 2.

eligibility.reason: The study compares student ideas collected in 2021 with separate GPT-4 pools generated by the researchers; study participants were not assigned to AI-assisted ideation (p. 10, Section 4). Randomization concerned the ideas shown to evaluators, not access to AI assistance (p. 12, Section 5). The original course had 50 students, but the number of distinct student authors represented among the 200 sampled ideas is not stated; criterion 2 is unclear and participants.n_analyzed remains null (p. 10, Section 4). Purchase intent and novelty were rated on the ideas, and similarity was computed on their text, so criterion 3 is met (pp. 12-15, Sections 5 and 6.1; pp. 17-18, Section 6.3). Core eligibility remains no because criterion 1 is not met; this is AI-versus-human context evidence.

one_line_finding: GPT-4 product ideas drew higher purchase intent than student ideas (46.4 percent zero-shot and 49.3 percent few-shot vs 40.4 percent, p. 13) but were rated less novel (36.7 and 36.1 percent vs 40.6 percent, p. 17) and were more similar to each other (mean cosine similarity 0.415 and 0.428 vs 0.221, Table 1, p. 15), and 35 of the top 40 ideas came from GPT-4 (Table 3, p. 20).
notes: The paper's Studies 1-3 analyze one corpus of 400 ideas, so the form records them as one study entry. Figure 1 (p. 13, purchase intent) prints box labels 'Mean: 0.41 Std: 0.117', 'Mean: 0.366 Std: 0.101', 'Mean: 0.361 Std: 0.111', which match the novelty figure (Figure 3, p. 18) and not the purchase-intent means in the text (40.4, 46.4, 49.3 percent); the recorded purchase-intent numbers come from the text.
